features.title: Built for analysts who need proof

cards.title: Cited answers
cards.body: Every figure Raynard gives you links back to the source it came from.

cards.title: Connect anything
cards.body: Send Raynard a link to an API’s docs and it can build the connection for you—no config files.

cards.title: Plain English, real numbers
cards.body: Ask questions the way you would ask a colleague. Get grounded numbers, not guesses.

cards.title: Native desktop app
cards.body: A desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows that keeps conversations, connections, and credentials under your control.

items.title: Ask about the thing that changed this morning
items.prompt: Is Nvidia down three days in a row? And what usually happens next?
items.body: Raynard checks today’s actual closes and works it out. A chatbot that half-remembers the web gives you a confident number and no way to check it.
bullets: Reads the live prices as they stand right now, not a summary of a page about them
Shows the closes it checked, so you can see the working
Ask a follow-up and it fetches again instead of guessing
items.mediaLabel: Placeholder for a live share-price answer screenshot

items.title: Ask about data no chatbot can reach
items.prompt: Does a glass of wine actually wreck my sleep? Check the last six months.
items.body: Your sleep, your training, your customers, your company’s own orders system. It sits behind a login, so no search engine has ever seen it.
bullets: Works the same on your business — “which customers cancelled last month, and what were they paying?”
Or on the internal API nobody ever built a dashboard for: paste the docs, approve the connection, ask the question
API keys live in your operating system’s keychain, and your chats stay on your own machine — there’s no Raynard server
items.mediaLabel: Placeholder for a private-account analysis screenshot

items.title: For when being wrong is expensive
items.prompt: Which of these can I put in the board deck? Show me where each number came from.
items.body: Every figure keeps the record it came from, so you can check it now, check it again next month, or hand someone else the whole thing.
bullets: Each number links back to the exact record behind it
The supporting data is saved alongside the answer, so it still checks out later
Send an answer as a link — no account needed to read it
items.mediaLabel: Placeholder for a cited answer with source links screenshot

items.title: The question that asks itself
items.prompt: Every Monday at 8, tell me whether last week’s sales were up or down on the same week last month — and which products moved.
items.body: Set it once and the answer is waiting when you open the app. Daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly, in your own time zone.
bullets: The comparison is worked out against live data every time, not carried over from last week’s answer
Lands in a chat of its own, or one you already have
Pause it, run it early, or change the question whenever you like
items.mediaLabel: Placeholder for a scheduled task and its result screenshot

items.title: And if it’s not on the list, just say so
items.prompt: Add World Bank data for me to chat with — it’s at data360.worldbank.org/en/api
items.body: Point Raynard at an API’s documentation and it writes the connection, tests it against the real thing, and keeps it for next time.
bullets: Builds and tests the connector from a prompt, after you approve it
Available in every chat from then on
Keep it on your own machine or share it

howItWorks.title: From question to receipt in three steps

steps.title: Point it at your data
steps.body: Paste a link to an API’s docs or request a data source. Raynard sets up the extension after you approve it.

steps.title: Ask in plain English
steps.body: No query language and no dashboard to build. Just type the question you actually have.

steps.title: Get answers with receipts
steps.body: Every number retains its source, so you can double-check the evidence before you rely on it.

cta.title: Ready to talk data?
cta.body: Connect your sources and start asking questions.
